subtitle: The Lowtowns and the Rust Market, the shadowed districts at the foot of Argentis, where the poor burn shards for light
canonNote: Canon (world_bible.md Geography; book1 ch.1, 3, 9, 13, 15-16, 20): Argentis is the capital, the Crown on the mountain white stone and gold, the Lowtowns at its base, sprawling and shadowed, filled with industry and poverty; the Rust Market, Sector 4, against the Forge District's walls under the smog of the High City's foundries, sells roasting skewered rat and cheap aether-spiced wine; the Rusty Spoon; the Iron Teeth; the Blind Seer's Antiquities; the Chemical River; red clay brick sewers; Weave-Eaters, against which salt and bone harpoons on amber rope serve and steel turns black and brittle; sparked children taken from the alleys; spent shards burned for light; Rule One of the Lowtowns. GAME-ONLY: every person, building, camp and quest here, the Holding House, the Shard-Burners' Yard and the reading that the shards are memory sifted from the slag (the Sludge-Tunnels' design). The game is set before Book 1: no purges, no Quarantine Wards, no burning of the Lowtowns; Seekers are only spoken of. Docs/ZONE_LOWTOWNS.md.
worldMapNote: At the foot of Argentis, just below the Crown, where the game map draws the capital at the centre of the land; the Lowtowns are not drawn on it, so the pin is provisional.
objectives: Find Toll-Reeve Edda Holt at the Gate Ward
Learn where the warrant's children were taken

landmarks.name: The Gate Ward
landmarks.text: Argentis's outer gate, standing open because nobody remembers how to shut it. The toll-house, the carters' yards, and the smell of the whole city coming the other way.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Argentis and its Lowtowns are CANON (world_bible.md Geography); the Gate Ward GAME-ONLY

landmarks.name: The Holding House
landmarks.text: Grey stone, barred windows, a heavy door. Children taken by warrant were kept here a night before they went up. It is empty now, and guarded anyway.

landmarks.name: The Rusty Spoon
landmarks.text: A decrepit establishment known for watered-down ale and high-stakes games. It smells like wet dog and stale beer. Triad at the back table, a ballad about a goat in the corner, and a brawl most nights. The chairs are missing an inch on one leg, most of them.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: the Rusty Spoon (book1 ch.1:9), its smell (ch.1:7), Triad (ch.1:45), the ballad (ch.1:59), Snivels (ch.1:105), the brawl and the front window (ch.1:107-121); its rooms and the rest of its people GAME-ONLY

landmarks.name: The Tenement Rows
landmarks.text: Brick terraces four storeys high, washing across the lanes, stoops, and puddles of questionable origin. Most of the Lowtowns live here, a family a room.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Lowtowns' poverty and puddles (world_bible.md; book1 ch.1:143); the Rows GAME-ONLY

landmarks.name: The Soup-Hall
landmarks.text: A little chapel of no particular god, turned to feeding the Rows. The god's chair is gone; a copper stands in its place.

landmarks.name: The Chemical River
landmarks.text: Black, slow and iridescent where the lamps catch it. Nothing natural lives in it. The barges are poled through it by people who try not to splash.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: the Chemical River through Argentis (book1 ch.15-16); its course here GAME-ONLY

landmarks.name: The Sett Bridge
landmarks.text: A brick bridge over the black river, its setts worn to ridges by carts. The Ward-watch keeps its west end.

landmarks.name: The Rag Bridge
landmarks.text: Rags hang off its parapets. Nobody hangs them and nobody takes them down.

landmarks.name: The Docks
landmarks.text: Honest labour: barges poled in and out, sacks and bales on backs, no cranes. The quays are timber, tarred black, and they creak.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: honest labour at the docks (book1 ch.3:17); the quays GAME-ONLY

landmarks.name: The Drain Courts
landmarks.text: Closed courts round old drain mouths of red clay brick. By day they are quiet. By night something comes up out of them.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: the sewers' red clay brick (book1 ch.9:47) and the Weave-Eaters (book1 ch.1:251); the courts GAME-ONLY

landmarks.name: The Rust Market
landmarks.text: Sector 4, under the Forge District's wall: covered stalls in a tangle of lanes, roasting skewered rat, cheap aether-spiced wine, and smog over everything. It does not sleep.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: the Rust Market, Sector 4 (book1 ch.3:3-9); its stalls and people GAME-ONLY

landmarks.name: The Blind Seer's Antiquities
landmarks.text: A clean shopfront of old things. Everyone in the Lowtowns knows not to ask about the back room.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: the Blind Seer's Antiquities (book1 ch.3:13); its back room is not entered

landmarks.name: The Iron Teeth's Warehouse
landmarks.text: A long brick warehouse with its doors shut. Up here the Iron Teeth are traders. What they are below is their own business.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: the Iron Teeth and their warehouse in the Rust Market (B1WB:26; book1 ch.7:21)

landmarks.name: The Shard-Burners' Yard
landmarks.text: The Lowtowns' dead-house. The poor buy back a shard of their own here, a night's light at a time.
landmarks.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY reading (the shards as burned memory, DUNGEON_DESIGN.md); spent shards as light are CANON (book1 ch.3:133-137)

landmarks.name: The Outfall
landmarks.text: Where the Forge District's drain comes out under the wall: a great arch of brick, an iron grating, and a smell like a hot coin. A sign says what everybody knows.
landmarks.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (the Sludge-Tunnels' door, DUNGEON_DESIGN.md, not yet open)

landmarks.name: The Forge District Gate
landmarks.text: Shut, barred from the far side. Smoke rolls over the wall from the chimney stacks beyond.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: the Forge District's walls (book1 ch.3:5); the gate shut until that zone opens (GAME-ONLY)

landmarks.name: Dead Man's Drop
landmarks.text: The lane runs on between blind brick walls and then simply stops. Past a snapped iron railing the street vanishes into the dark of the Under-City, loose stones clicking away into it, and the wind comes up cold. Three stories down a thick, rotting fungal net hangs across the shaft; under it, nothing you can see.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: Dead Man's Drop in the Rust Market's lanes, 'where the street simply vanished into the yawning, bottomless abyss of the Under-City' (book1 ch.1:313), the 'thick, rotting fungal-net suspended three stories down' (ch.1:347); the railing, the lane's name and the iron rungs out GAME-ONLY

landmarks.name: The drowned vaults
landmarks.text: Rubble-stone vaults under the Rust Market, a black canal down the middle and a causeway along it, green mould glowing on the arches. The Warrens' upper edge: smugglers, a fence, and a way under the river.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Warrens' drowned lower levels, a causeway along a black-water canal under high arched ceilings, faint green light (book1 ch.6:41, ch.6:129, ch.6:185-187); here the Warrens' upper edge under the Rust Market (conflict 4); the vaults' plan GAME-ONLY

residents.name: Edda Holt
residents.title: Toll-Reeve
stories: Thirty years I've kept the toll-book. Carts, bales, pilgrims, a man with a bear once. You write what comes through the gate and you don't ask what it's for.
The warrant page I keep in the back of the book, where the Council's men can't see me reading it twice.
My mother said the gate used to shut at dusk. Now it never shuts. Nobody ever decided that. It just stopped closing.

residents.name: Ludo Brand
residents.title: Carter
stories: I've carted up the south-east road from Oakhaven every week since I could hold the reins. Grain up, rags and pots down. The road doesn't care which.
Somebody's been cutting bales off the barges at night and selling them back to me in the morning. My own bales. At a price.

residents.name: Mother Sall
residents.title: Keeper of the Rusty Spoon
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the books name no keeper of the Rusty Spoon, only its bartender, Snivels Gear-Grinder (b1 ch.1:105), who stands beside her; nothing in them contradicts her, so she keeps the house
stories: The ale's watered because the water's cheaper than the ale. Everybody knows. Nobody complains. That's the Spoon's whole secret.
Chairs get broken in here most nights. I keep a cellar of legs. Nobody's ever asked why there are so many legs.
I don't take sides at my tables. I take coin. The games are high and the stakes are other people's.

residents.name: Gorm Rock-Wall
residents.title: Lowtown Muscle
residents.canonStatus: CANON: Gorm Rock-Wall, Valen's orc, at the Spoon (b1 ch.1:21-25); "Ale tastes like rust" (ch.1:133); the pier and the fishing pole (ch.1:153-159); he dug a boy out of Hallow's Creek's ash ten years before the book (ch.19:39; the boy unnamed here, Chris's conflict 7); the sap-root GAME-ONLY
stories: The ale here tastes like rust. I drink it anyway. You get used to rust in the Lowtowns. You get used to most things. Sap-root for a split knuckle. Chew it, spit it on, don't look at it. Orc remedy. Works on you lot too, mostly.
My mother told me of a pier in the north where the water runs clear and you can just sit. One day I'll have a pier. And a fishing pole that isn't scrap wire.
Ten years back I dug a boy out of the ash at Hallow's Creek. Stone all round him, and him still five years old after forty years under. Don't ask me how. I don't.

residents.name: Snivels Gear-Grinder
residents.title: Bartender of the Rusty Spoon
residents.canonStatus: CANON: Snivels Gear-Grinder, the Rusty Spoon's goblin bartender (b1 ch.1:105), who knows the forgotten eastern paths and the Reach's sweetest cider (ch.4:13-15); in the book he is lost later, so before Book 1 he pours (Chris's conflict 9: "snivel is fine"); his lines GAME-ONLY. He stands at the bar's front end: the gap behind the bar is too narrow to walk
stories: Snivels Gear-Grinder, at your service. Don't lean on the bar. It isn't holding itself up so much as remembering how. Every brawl in here starts at the card table and ends at my vodka shelf. Every single one.
The east roads? Everybody says they're gone. They're not gone. They're forgotten. There's a difference, and I'm the one who still knows where it is.
There's a village out in the Reach makes the sweetest apple cider you ever tasted. If they ever stop, I'll have to start boiling my own boots.

residents.name: Ottie Swale
residents.title: The Corner Drunk
residents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the drunk in the Spoon's corner butchering The Ballad of the One-Legged Goat (b1 ch.1:59); his name and lines GAME-ONLY (the book gives the song's title only, so no verses are written)
stories: You want a song? I've got one song. It's a good one. It's about a goat.
The Ballad of the One-Legged Goat has forty verses. I know three. I sing them in a different order every night so nobody notices.
Don't sit in at the card table. I sat in at the card table once. Look at me.

residents.name: Gytha Pell
residents.title: Mother
stories: My Ysa sparked over the washing. A little light in her hands, like a moth's. I told her to put it out. As if she could.
They came for her with a paper. A paper. I can't read, but I know a paper is worth more than a girl, up there.
I keep her cup on the sill. The neighbours think I'm mad. Let them. It's a cup. It's hers.

residents.name: Brother Aldo
residents.title: Keeper of the Soup-Hall
stories: This was a chapel once. Nobody remembers to what. I took the god's chair out and put a copper in its place. The copper does more good.
Bones, turnips and whatever the market throws out at closing. I call it soup. The Rows call it Thursday.
I counted the children at the tables before the warrant came. I count them now. I don't tell anyone the difference.

residents.name: Old Wulf
residents.title: Former Militia Sergeant
stories: Lowtown militia, twenty years. We had bucklers that rusted if you looked at them and spears we pulled off a scrap heap. We were the only ones who came when the drains rose.
Steel's no good on a Weave-Eater. Goes black and breaks like old glass. Salt's what you want. Salt, and something with a rope on it.
They disbanded us. Not enough coin for watchmen, the Council said. Then they hired warders for the Holding House out of the same coin.

residents.name: Tibb Marrow
residents.title: Salt-Seller
stories: Rock salt, sea salt, grey salt off the Ash-Walkers' carts. Throw it at what comes out of the drains and watch it go white. Two crowns a twist.
People laugh at a salt-seller till the lamps go out in their lane. Then they come to me in their nightshirts.

residents.name: Ketta Rune
residents.title: Bone-Harpooner
stories: Bone for the head, amber for the rope. The old craft. Steel goes through them; bone catches. Don't ask me why. My grandmother didn't know either.
I learned it off an Ash-Walker who came down to sell salt and stayed to drink. He paid his slate in lessons.
A good harpoon pins an Eater the way a nail pins a shadow. It shouldn't work. It does.

residents.name: Odo Sark
residents.title: Clerk of the Antiquities
stories: The Antiquities buys and sells old things. The back room is not for sale and not for looking at. That's the only rule. It's a good rule.
I keep the front of the shop very clean. Clean fronts are restful. People stop asking questions about clean fronts.

residents.name: Grimbold
residents.title: Iron Teeth Factor
stories: Up here in the market the Teeth are traders, friend. What we are below is our business. Buy something or move along.
Every lamp in the Lowtowns burns a shard, and every shard comes through somebody's hands. Mostly ours. Think on that when you light yours.

residents.name: Osric Fenn
residents.title: Shard-Burner
stories: A shard is a little light that used to be somebody. We buy them back for the families, when the families can pay. A night's light, a shard. Sometimes two.
Burn one wrong and what's left walks. We keep those in the cellar. I don't go down there after dark, and I'm the one with the key.
My mother keeps the old Fenn house in the Rows. She thinks I sell lamp-oil. Let her.

residents.name: Hale Dunning
residents.title: Ward-Watch
stories: The Ward-watch: two of us on the bridges, a lamp each and no pay worth the name. We watch. That's the job. We watch.
Old Wulf drills us when he's sober. He says the militia stood when the drains rose. I believe him. I've seen the drains.

residents.name: Ebba Strand
residents.title: Ward-Watch
stories: Rag Bridge's mine. Rags hang off it because the wind brings them. Nobody hangs them. Nobody takes them down.
At night I count the lamps on Weir Lane. When one goes out I don't go and look. I count again in the morning.

residents.name: Rudd Crake
residents.title: Dock Ganger
stories: Honest labour at the docks. Lift, carry, pole, sleep. The barges go down to the river towns and back with whatever's cheap.
No cranes on my quays. Backs and ropes. A crane's a thing that breaks and someone has to pay for. A back mends.

residents.name: Nan Tallow
residents.title: Skewer-Seller
stories: Roasting skewered rat, two a copper, three if you don't ask. They're rats. They're hot. That's the whole of the promise.
Smog makes the fat spit. I've a burn on every finger. My mother had the same burns. It's the family trade.

residents.name: Meg Brisk
residents.title: Wine-Seller
stories: Aether-spiced wine. It's cheap, it's hot, and nobody knows what the aether is. Don't drink the bottom of the jug.
The High City throws its old wine down the drains. Some of it ends up here, and some of that ends up in my jugs. Waste not.

residents.name: Wynn Madder
residents.title: Dyer
stories: Madder for red, woad for blue, weld for yellow, soot for everything else. The Lowtowns wear a lot of everything else.
My arms are blue to the elbow and red past it. The children call me the Flag.

residents.name: Wenna Slate
residents.title: Rag-and-Pot Seller
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
stories: Rags by weight, pots by the hole. A pot with one hole is half price. Two holes, it's a sieve, and sieves cost more.
My man went to the Forge District for the wages. He sends a coin a month and a letter I can't read. I keep both.

residents.name: Jory Clink
residents.title: Pie-Seller
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
stories: Pease pudding, a ha'penny. Rat pie, a penny. The rat's the dear part. Don't ask me why.
The Council's men buy my pies on the quiet. They say it's for the warders. The warders say it's for the Council's men.

residents.name: Sabe Murrow
residents.title: Pot-Mender
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
stories: Bring it back cracked and I'll mend it twice. Bring it back cracked three times and I'll say it was never a pot.
There's a shard-burner two stalls down sells light by the hour. I sell light by the candle. The candle doesn't remember anything.

residents.name: Doll Patchet
residents.title: Haggler
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
stories: Five for the boots or I walk. I won't walk far, mind. They're good boots.
You hear things in a market. Who's selling, who's buying, whose child went missing in the night. Mostly you hear the price of eels.

residents.name: Ivo Tamsin
residents.title: Rag-Buyer
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
stories: Forty years I've bought rags. You know a family by its rags. Patches on patches is a family that's holding on.
When I was a boy the smog came down at dusk and lifted at dawn. Now it doesn't lift. You stop noticing. That's the worst of it.

residents.name: Fen Ashlock
residents.title: Porter
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
stories: I carry for anyone. Sacks to the barges, crates up from the docks, a drunk home now and then. A drunk's the heaviest.
No carts past the Gate Ward by day, the Council says. So it's backs. Mine's as good as any cart and it doesn't need greasing.

residents.name: Pip Hensey
residents.title: Errand-Runner
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
stories: A copper and I'll run it anywhere. Two and I won't read it. I can't read anyway, but you don't know that.
My sister sparked. Little lights, on the stairs. Mam says don't talk about it. So I don't. I'm not talking now.

residents.name: Rook Garran
residents.title: Idler
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
stories: I'm not idling. I'm watching the market for a friend. The friend's me. I'm watching for a cheap pie.
The Spoon opens at noon and so do I. Till then I lean. A man needs a wall in the Lowtowns.

residents.name: The Merchant of Nothing
residents.title: Seller of Jars
residents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the street vendor of the Lowtowns' tale 'The Merchant of Nothing' (lore_stories.md #9), his words his own; out only at night in the market that 'did not sleep' (book1 ch.3:5); his stall GAME-ONLY
stories: You want to buy a jar of The Wasting? Genuine article, pulled straight from the edge of the void. Look at it. See how empty it is? That's premium nothingness, that is.
Most nothing you buy in this market is cut with air or shadow. Not mine. Pure, unadulterated non-existence. Don't open it indoors, or you'll erase the cat.
Ten gold sovereigns. No refunds if the jar stops existing before you get home. Day trade? No. Nothing sells best in the dark, where folk can't see how little's in it.

residents.name: Abel Snuff
residents.title: Candlemaker
residents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the candlemaker of the Lowtowns' tale 'The Glitch' (lore_stories.md #6), his blue light-butterflies; his name and his night stall GAME-ONLY
stories: I tried to light a candle the other night. Same striker I've used twenty years. Spark hit the wick, and instead of fire I got butterflies. Little blue butterflies made of light.
They fly round a while and then pop into smoke that smells of sulphur. There, see? That one. The magic is sick, friend. It's confused, like a dog that doesn't know its master any more.
One day it bites, the next day it licks your hand. And one day it's going to bite our throats out. Buy a candle. They still burn, mostly.

residents.name: Mother Gant
residents.title: Card-Reader
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the card-reader and her chalk ring in the Night Market; the Triad's suits, Wyrms and Coins, and the three Kings that are the Crown are CANON (book1 ch.1:47, 55-57)
stories: Step into the chalk, love, and keep your feet inside it. Three cards. Wyrms for what's coming, Coins for what it'll cost you.
Ace of Wyrms. Somebody near you is going to fall a long way and land on something soft. Don't laugh. It happens down here more than you'd think.
Three Kings. The Crown. Nobody beats the Crown, love; you just keep out of its way. That'll be a copper, and another for the chalk.

residents.name: Dace Mottle
residents.title: Iron Teeth runner
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: an Iron Teeth runner holding the day's corner (Lowtowns pick 12, the turf by the day); the Iron Teeth and their warehouse kept as neutral ground are CANON (book1 ch.7:21; B1WB:26)
stories: Teeth's corner today. Bridge foot's ours from sunup to sunup. You cross, you cross polite.
Tomorrow it's somebody else's. That's the trick of it: nobody holds a corner long enough to get greedy.

residents.name: Rusk Hollin
residents.title: Iron Teeth runner
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: an Iron Teeth runner holding the day's corner (Lowtowns pick 12, the turf by the day); the Iron Teeth and their warehouse kept as neutral ground are CANON (book1 ch.7:21; B1WB:26)
stories: Carts pay the Ward-watch at the far end. This end, they nod to us. Costs less.
See the teeth on the setts? Ochre. Same as on the warehouse roof. Means we're about.

residents.name: Vell Tarrow
residents.title: Iron Teeth runner
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: an Iron Teeth runner holding the day's corner (Lowtowns pick 12, the turf by the day); the Iron Teeth and their warehouse kept as neutral ground are CANON (book1 ch.7:21; B1WB:26)
stories: Teeth Lane. Funny how it's only ours one day in three.
The warehouse? Neutral ground, friend. Nobody's turf. Not even ours. That's why it's still standing.

residents.name: Brig Carrow
residents.title: Iron Teeth runner
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: an Iron Teeth runner holding the day's corner (Lowtowns pick 12, the turf by the day); the Iron Teeth and their warehouse kept as neutral ground are CANON (book1 ch.7:21; B1WB:26)
stories: Keep your hands where I can see them and your coin where I can't.
Up at the warehouse we trade. Down here on the corner we watch. Different jobs.

residents.name: Sloe Mackin
residents.title: Iron Teeth runner
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: an Iron Teeth runner holding the day's corner (Lowtowns pick 12, the turf by the day); the Iron Teeth and their warehouse kept as neutral ground are CANON (book1 ch.7:21; B1WB:26)
stories: The weir's ours today. Walk the crest if you like. Mind the plank over the sluice; it's had a few in.
Sluice-keeper lifts the boards with a hook-pole when the sludge backs up. We just stand here and look like we mean it.

residents.name: Jink Pellow
residents.title: Iron Teeth runner
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: an Iron Teeth runner holding the day's corner (Lowtowns pick 12, the turf by the day); the Iron Teeth and their warehouse kept as neutral ground are CANON (book1 ch.7:21; B1WB:26)
stories: Eels come up under the weir when the boards go in. Don't feed them. Don't be fed to them.
Ochre on the stones, a banner on the pole. Tomorrow we're on another corner and this is just a weir again.

residents.name: Ottie Brack
residents.title: Fence
residents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: a fence (the drowned levels are 'a haven for smugglers, fences', book1 ch.6:185); the black skiff at an iron-ringed pier CANON-EXPANDED (ch.6:203)
stories: You came down the stair on your own feet, so you can go back up it on them. Buy or don't. The canal doesn't listen and neither do I.
Everything on my boat fell off something. Off a wagon, off a barge, off a dead man. Nobody up there misses it enough to come down here.

Hear that? Water on a hull. Some nights a crew sings coming up the canal, old sea songs nobody down here has any business knowing. The Teeth keep the pier. I pay them, they stand there looking like teeth. Don't start anything on my planks.

stories.name: Aldred Coke
lines: The market hearth's bellows are my arms. No engine in the Lowtowns works as cheap as a smith who needs to eat.
Slag-iron. The foundries throw it out; I beat it into nails. Their waste, my bread.

stories.name: Hild Barrow
lines: I was a field-hand once, out past the gate. Then the fields went to the Council's tenants. Now I drink in the Spoon and remember barley.
My Leof says we'll go back out one day. He's been saying it eleven years.

stories.name: Cuth Penny
lines: Penny's stall: nails, buttons, string, knives, and whatever fell off a barge. Don't ask which is which.
I lodge at the Mallows'. Wat makes my purses. I sell them back to people who've had theirs cut.

stories.name: Elga Sump
lines: The oven's lit at four. Smog bread: it rises grey and nobody minds. Flour comes up from Oakhaven on Ludo's cart.
My sister tans hides by the river. Between us we smell of the two best and worst things in the Lowtowns.

stories.name: Brand Tolley
lines: You want to know who's sleeping with whose husband in the Rows? Three crowns. You want to know who's been taken? Free. Everybody knows.
Sigga says I talk too much. Sigga talks more. She just does it quieter.

stories.name: Wyn Garth
lines: I used to run game down from the woods past Oakhaven. No woods here. I lodge with Osgar and drink his cider and wait for something to hunt.
Rats, if you're hungry. Gutter-hounds, if you're brave. I'm neither tonight.

stories.name: Osgar Rook
lines: First cup's for the dead. Second's for the living. Third's for the Council, so it can choke on it.
I had a shop once, on Gate Street. A Seeker walked in looking for somebody. I've been drinking since. I don't remember the shop much.

stories.name: Tilda Grime
lines: Lamp-tag! You touch a lamp-post and you're safe. If you're not touching one the Eaters get you. That's the rule.
My friend Ysa sparked. Her hands went bright. Then she went away. Mum says don't say her name.

stories.name: Edwy Larch
lines: Cut timber in the north for a lumber-master till my back went. Now I pull cinder-beams out of the fallen terraces for burning. Same work, sadder trees.
The Barrows let me the cupboard under the stair. It's dry. In the Lowtowns that's a palace.

stories.name: Mabb Soot
lines: Soot-wort grows where nothing should: in the gutters, on the ash heaps. It's good for a cough. Everybody here has a cough.
Lamp-lichen glows by the drains. Pick it at night and your hands shine till morning. Don't eat it.

stories.name: Leof Crane
lines: Fields, Hild says. Barley, Hild says. Hild's never weeded a row in her life. I have. I'm happy with the Spoon.
My brother went for a watchman and they gave him a lamp and no pay. He gave the lamp back.

stories.name: Gisla Fenn
lines: My Osric sells lamp-oil in the south of the market. Good boy. Always smells of smoke. I don't ask.
I've lived in the Rows seventy years. The terraces were new brick once. I remember the colour. Red, like a cheek.

stories.name: Ricca Stave
lines: I worked the mills upriver till the mills stopped wanting people. Now I lodge with old Gisla and carry for anyone with a copper.
The river's black because the High City's sick, my father said. He said it like it was weather.

stories.name: Wat Mallow
lines: Gutter-hound hide makes a good purse. Tough, and nobody wants to steal a thing that smells like that.
Mabb's my wife. She picks the weeds, I tan the hounds. We keep a clean house anyway.

stories.name: Duna Slake
lines: The tanning yard's by the river because the river can't smell any worse. Neither can I.
Elga bakes, I tan. When we visit Mother we stand at opposite ends of the room.

stories.name: Sigga Nail
lines: Brand talks. I listen. That's how we know everything between us.
The warders at the Holding House drink in the Spoon on their nights off. They don't talk about the children. They don't have to. They drink like men who don't.

secrets.name: Rule One, Chalked
secrets.text: Chalked on the brick under the bridge's west end, in a dozen hands, the same line over and over, the oldest rubbed nearly away.
secrets.clue: Under the west end of the sett-paved bridge, low on the brick where the watch can't see, somebody keeps chalking the same rule.
secrets.hint: Hale Dunning says there's a line chalked under the west end of his bridge, low down. Every child in the Lowtowns learns it before their letters.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON: Rule One of the Lowtowns (book1 ch.1:257); the chalk GAME-ONLY

secrets.name: The Soup-Hall Slate
secrets.text: A slate hung by the old chapel's door, chalked and rubbed and chalked again: who ate, who paid in turnips, who owes nothing because nobody could make them.
secrets.clue: By the door of the chapel that feeds the Rows, a slate keeps count of who ate and who paid.
secrets.hint: Brother Aldo keeps a slate by his door. He says if you want to know the Rows, read who ate this week. And who didn't come.

secrets.name: The Burners' Tally
secrets.text: A board nailed up behind the racks: names, a date, a number of nights. The numbers are small. Some names have a second date, and nothing after.
secrets.clue: Behind the racks where the shards glow, a board is nailed up: names, dates, and how many nights each bought.
secrets.hint: Osric Fenn says the tally behind his racks is the truest book in the Lowtowns. Names and nights. He doesn't say whose nights.
secrets.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (the shards as burned memory: the Sludge-Tunnels' reading)

secrets.name: The Price-Board
secrets.text: A board leaned against a post, prices chalked and crossed out and chalked higher, a smear of soot over the lot.
secrets.clue: Where the long stalls meet the lane, a chalked board of prices leans on a post, every price crossed out and written higher.
secrets.hint: Nan Tallow says the price-board by the long stalls is a history of the Lowtowns. Read it top to bottom and you can watch everyone get poorer.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON: skewered rat and aether-spiced wine sold in the Rust Market (book1 ch.3:7); the board GAME-ONLY

secrets.name: An Old Toll-Book Page
secrets.prompt: Pull the page from the crack
secrets.text: A page torn from a toll-book years ago and stuffed in a crack of the wall's inner face, the ink run, the hand neat and frightened.
secrets.clue: Inside the city's wall, just south of the gate, a page from an old toll-book is stuffed in a crack of the brick.
secrets.hint: Edda Holt says the reeve before her tore a page out of the book and hid it in the wall south of the gate. She has never gone to look. She says you might.

secrets.name: A Docker in the Drain
secrets.text: Bones in a docker's leather apron, half in the black water by a drain mouth, one hand still closed round a twist of salt that did him no good. A note is buttoned in the apron.
secrets.clue: In the deepest of the courts, by a drain's mouth, a docker lies half in the black water with salt in his fist.
secrets.hint: Rudd Crake says one of his gang went into the far courts with a twist of salt to see what took his sister. He didn't come back to the quay.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Weave-Eaters and salt (book1 ch.20); the docker GAME-ONLY

secrets.name: The Militia Roll
secrets.text: A board of names cut with a knife into the wall by the well, the old militia's roll. Some names have a stroke through them. The last is Wulf's, with no stroke.
secrets.clue: Cut into the brick by the well in the Rows, a roll of names, some struck through, the last not.
secrets.hint: Old Wulf says the names by the well are the militia's. He cut them himself. He'll cut his own stroke when it's time, he says, not before.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON: the former Lowtown militia (book1 ch.20:127); the roll GAME-ONLY

secrets.name: The Harpooner's Count
secrets.prompt: Untie the strip and read it
secrets.text: A strip of amber-dyed cloth tied to a stall post, knotted all along: a knot for every Eater pinned, the old way, and a few words stitched at the end.
secrets.clue: On a stall post in the market's heart, a strip of amber cloth is knotted end to end.
secrets.hint: Ketta Rune says her grandmother's count is tied to a post in the market where she can see it. A knot for every one pinned. She's added three.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON: bone harpoons on amber rope (book1 ch.20:177-191); the count GAME-ONLY

secrets.name: The Spoon's Slate
secrets.text: A slate on a nail round the side of the inn, by the cellar flap: the Spoon's debts, and a column headed BROKEN CHAIRS, very long.
secrets.clue: Round the west side of the inn, by the cellar flap, a slate of debts hangs on a nail.
secrets.hint: Mother Sall says her slate of debts hangs round the side by the cellar. Everybody owes. She says reading it is the best entertainment in the Lowtowns.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Rusty Spoon (book1 ch.1:9); the slate GAME-ONLY

secrets.name: A Warder Who Asked
secrets.text: A man in a warder's grey coat, face down behind the house where they hold people, a long time dead. Nobody moved him. His orders are folded in his glove.
secrets.clue: Behind the grey stone house by the gate, where the warders don't walk, one of their own lies face down.
secrets.hint: Sigga Nail says one of the warders asked a question about the children, and nobody saw him after. Behind the grey house, she says. Nobody goes round the back.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Council's hired men; Seekers' warrants spoken of only; GAME-ONLY

secrets.name: Where the Smog Thins
secrets.text: For a moment the smog thins and there it is, far up the mountain in the north-east: white stone and gold, towers and a dome and a spire like a needle. The Crown. It doesn't look real from down here. It isn't meant to.
secrets.clue: In the far north of the town, past the river, there is a place the smog thins enough to see the High City.
secrets.hint: Ebba Strand says if you go north past her bridge, to the open yards at the top of the town, the smog thins some days and you can see the Crown. She goes there when she's off. Just to look.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON: the Crown, white stone and gold (world_bible.md Geography; book1 ch.3: the smog of the High City's foundries); the lookout GAME-ONLY

secrets.name: Marks on the Court Wall
secrets.text: Scratched into the brick at shoulder height: a row of strokes in fives, and over them, in a militia hand, NIGHTS WE HELD THE COURT.
secrets.clue: In the court of the tanners' drains, someone cut a tally of nights into the brick at shoulder height.
secrets.hint: Old Wulf says the militia held the tanners' court against the drains for a winter. They cut the nights in the wall. He can't bring himself to count them.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the former Lowtown militia (book1 ch.20:127); the marks GAME-ONLY

secrets.name: The Lamp-Shrine
secrets.prompt: Leave a copper by the lamp
secrets.text: A niche in a quay-side wall with a lamp in it that somebody always keeps lit, and under it a dish of coppers and shard-dust. No god's face. Just the lamp.
secrets.clue: On the riverside walk, in a niche in the wall, a lamp somebody always keeps lit sits over a dish of coppers.
secrets.hint: Rudd Crake says the dockers keep a lamp lit in the wall along the quays. A copper in the dish for the river. He says it's not for any god. It's for the lamp.

secrets.name: Grey-Bell
secrets.text: In the ash behind the dead-house, where the burners tip the cinders, a few pale flowers hang their heads: grey bells, with a light in them like a held breath.
secrets.clue: Behind the house where the dead are burned for light, pale flowers grow in the tipped cinders.
secrets.hint: Mabb Soot says grey-bell grows only where the burners tip their cinders, behind the dead-house. She won't pick it. She says it remembers.

secrets.name: Carvings Under the Moss
secrets.text: Under a skin of glowing green moss the rubble gives way to older stone, cut deep with patterns too fine for anyone who ever worked a drain. The moss pulses over them like a slow heartbeat.
secrets.clue: Somewhere in the crawl from the courts to the river the walls glow green, and under the glow the stone is older than the drains.
secrets.hint: Courts kids say if you scrape the green moss in the old crawl there's writing under it. Nobody can read it. Nobody tries twice.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: deep, intricate carvings beneath the pulsing bioluminescent moss (book1 ch.9:55); this wall GAME-ONLY
